What's New
June 2026
New Badge: First Video Post
Post your first video to the feed and earn the new First Video Post badge — a photo won’t do it, this one’s for bringing your watches to life in motion.
Add to Wishlist from a Photo
Spotted a grail in the wild? On your Wishlist, tap Add from Photo, snap or pick a picture, and we’ll identify the watch and pre-fill the brand, model, and reference for you. Just review, add a price or link if you like, and save.
Featured Posts
From time to time we’ll spotlight a standout post at the top of the feed, marked with a small ★ Featured tag. It’s our way of surfacing great watches and stories from the community.
Earn Your Weekend
Log every weekday (Mon–Fri) and you’ve earned the weekend — Saturday and Sunday won’t break your streak, and you don’t need to log them. Show up all week, then take the weekend off. Logging a weekend still counts as a bonus, and your streak calendar marks earned rest days with a small dot.
Occasion & Strap on Posts
When you tag a watch in a post, you can now add the occasion and which strap you’re wearing — tucked behind a small “Add occasion & strap” link so the composer stays light. We also tidied up the date picker on the Track screen: quick Today and Yesterday chips, with a Pick date option for anything further back.
Achievements in Your Feed
The badges you earn now show up in your feed, so friends can see your milestones and react. Earn one while logging a wear or posting and it appears right on that post; earn one another way and it gets its own card. You’re in control — switch it off anytime under Profile → Notifications → “Share achievements to feed.”
New Badge: Daily Double
Wear two different watches in the same day to earn the new Daily Double badge — for the days when one just isn’t enough.
Wear Streaks
A streak counter now lives in the top bar — the number of days in a row you’ve logged a wear. Tap it to open a calendar of every day you logged, with your current and best streak. And streak freezes have your back: miss a single day and a freeze automatically covers it so one slip doesn’t reset you. You start with two and earn one back for every seven days you log.
Dramatically More Accurate Measurements
We rebuilt the microphone timegrapher from the ground up — new tick detection, a steadier beat-error reading, and a smarter sense of when a measurement has truly settled. Validated across hundreds of calibrations against a professional reference, readings now track much more closely to a pro machine and stay consistent run to run, so the same watch reads the same. For the most reliable result, measure in a quiet spot with your watch in a consistent position.
Advanced Measure Settings
Tap the ⚙ gear on the Measure screen to fine-tune how readings are taken. Pick an environment preset — Quiet Room, Noisy Environment, or Weak Signal — or adjust Sensitivity and Convergence Speed yourself to get a reliable reading from trickier watches.
Share Any of Your Posts
You can now share your own posts no matter who they’re for — not just public ones. Public posts open a rich preview link anyone can see. For Followers and Close Friends posts, the link opens privately in WRotate and only shows the post to people you actually shared it with, so nothing leaks to anyone else.
May 2026
Delete Comments
Changed your mind? Tap the ⋮ menu on any comment to delete it. You can remove your own comments anywhere, and as the owner of a post you can remove any comment on it.
Multi-Image Posts
Posts now support up to 6 photos. Select multiple images at once or add more with the + button. Drag thumbnails to reorder — the first image is your hero shot. In the feed, tap any thumbnail to preview it, or tap the hero to open a fullscreen swipe viewer with dots and arrow navigation.
Achievement Badges
Earn badges as you use WRotate — post your first wrist shot, log 7 days in a row, measure your first watch, and more. Badges appear on your profile and are visible to everyone who visits it.
Timegrapher Accuracy Improvements
Better tick detection, improved BPH correction, and smarter phase recovery reduce false readings and help measurements converge faster — especially in noisy environments.
April 2026
Enhance Your Collection
Tap Enhance on any watch to auto-fill specs, dimensions, caliber, history, and background — powered by AI. Or tap the ☆ button in your collection header to enhance all your watches at once. Review results per watch and save individually or all at once.
Smarter Photo Identification
Add from Photo is powered by a new model with substantially better image recognition. Watches are detected in seconds, then each one is identified individually with high accuracy — brand, model, reference, and specs.
Add All & Quick Add
After a photo identifies multiple watches, tap Add All to save them to your collection in one go. Each card also has a quick Add button for instant saves, or Edit to review details first.
Market Values
See what your watches are worth with AI-based valuations. Open a watch and tap Check Value, or use Update Prices (the $ button) to check your entire collection at once. Values are tracked over time so you can see how your collection’s worth changes.
Share to WRotate
Share a photo from your camera roll and AI identifies your watch. Use the share sheet from Photos or any app to send an image directly to WRotate.
Timegrapher — Improved Accuracy
The audio timegrapher has been tuned for more reliable measurements. Place your watch on the iPhone microphone and measure its accuracy in seconds per day — just like a professional timegrapher.
March 2026
Reliability & Error Handling
Editing a post now rolls back changes if the server save fails, so your feed stays consistent. Club creation and user unblocking also handle errors gracefully with clear feedback.
Accessibility Improvements
Screen readers now get proper page headings and navigation landmarks across all tabs. Every page has a semantic heading structure for easier keyboard and assistive-technology navigation.
Post Pics Toggle
A new toggle on the Collection page lets you swap watch photos for your latest wrist shots. Each card shows the most recent post photo for that watch — toggle off to go back to the standard image.
Richer Email Notifications
Comment and mention email notifications now include the actual comment text in a styled quote block, so you can see what was said without opening the app.
Profile Posts Grid
Your profile now shows an Instagram-style 3×3 photo grid of your recent posts and wears, right below your collection. Tap any cell to jump to that post in the feed.
Report & Block
Tap the three-dot menu on any post to report it or block the user. You can also report a specific comment from the menu. Reported content is immediately removed from feeds while it’s reviewed.
Content Moderation
All posts and comments are checked against community guidelines. Flagged content is hidden from feeds and reviewed by an admin, who can confirm the removal or restore the content.
Terms of Use
New and existing users are asked to accept the Terms of Use, which cover community standards, content policies, and account rules. You can review them any time from the Help page.
Pull to Refresh
On the Feed, pull down to refresh your timeline — just like a native app. A spinner animates as you pull, and the latest posts load when you release.
Edit Post: Change Tagged Watch
When editing a post, you can now add, change, or remove the tagged watch. Forgot to tag a watch when you posted? Just edit the post and pick one from your collection.
Post a Photo, Auto-Log Your Wear
When you post a wrist shot from the Feed, AI recognizes which watch you’re wearing and matches it to your collection. The wear log is added automatically — just tap “Not this watch” if it gets it wrong.
Add Watches from Photo
Snap a photo of a single watch or a collection flat-lay and AI identifies each one. Brand, model, and reference are pre-filled so you can review and save in seconds.
Unified Photo Picker
Every photo action — posting, logging a wear, snap-to-track, adding a watch — now shows the same native menu: take a photo, choose from library, or pick a file.
Track Page: Recently Worn First
The watch selector on the Track page now sorts by most recently worn, so the watch on your wrist is always near the top.
Smarter Recommendations
Daily watch picks now factor in your ranking preferences, use-case habits, how new a purchase is, and watches that haven’t been getting enough wrist time. Tags like Dress or Dive also match to the right occasion.
iOS App & Push Notifications
WRotate is now available as an iOS app. Get push notifications when someone likes your wear, comments on your post, sends a follow request, or invites you to a club.
Clubs
Create or join clubs around brands, styles, or anything else. Invite members, manage roles, and share watches with your community.
@Mentions & Pinned Comments
Tag anyone with @username in comments and posts — they'll get notified instantly. The most-liked comment now pins to the top of each thread.
Close Friends Privacy
New “Close Friends” visibility option for individual watches, your collection, and your wishlist. Share only with people you trust most.
Feed Improvements
Feed loads faster with parallel queries and shows a loading skeleton instead of a blank screen. If something goes wrong, you’ll see a clear error with a retry button instead of silence.
Better Image Handling
Unsupported photo formats like HEIC are detected with a clear error message and suggestion to use JPG, PNG, or WebP. No more broken image previews.
UI Polish
Modals are properly centered on mobile, the bottom nav has better spacing for iPhones with home indicators, and the edit modal got visual refinements.
Smarter Sync
Cloud sync now only uploads changes you actually made instead of your entire collection every time. Faster saves, less data usage.
Offline Support
If you lose connection, a banner lets you know and your changes are saved locally. Everything syncs automatically when you’re back online.
Email Notifications
Get email alerts for comments, follows, friend requests, mentions, and club activity. Toggle each category on or off in the Notifications section on your profile.
Performance & Reliability
Profiles and club pages load faster with parallel queries. Feed fetches only the columns it needs. Graceful error handling throughout — background errors surface clear messages instead of silent failures.
Security
Hardened input escaping, query timeouts prevent hung requests, debounced saves reduce data writes, and graceful session expiry handling.

How to Measure
Measure Your Watch's Accuracy
1
Find a quiet spot
Background noise interferes with tick detection. A quiet room works best.
2
Position the watch
Place the watch touching the iPhone microphone (bottom edge, next to the charging port).
3
Tap Measure and hold still
Keep the watch steady — measuring usually takes 30–60 seconds (up to 90). It auto-stops once it has a confident reading.

Help & Guide

Building Your Collection
1
Quick add: tap "From Photo"
Take a photo of a single watch or a whole collection flat-lay. AI identifies each watch, then pre-fills the add form with brand, model, and reference number. Review and save — the fastest way to build your collection.
2
Or add manually: tap "+ Add Watch"
Opens the add watch form. Fill it manually or use the URL fetch shortcut below.
3
Paste a product page URL and tap Fetch
Go to the brand's website (rolex.com, omegawatches.com, seikowatches.com…), open the exact watch page, copy the URL, and paste it in. Fetch fills in brand, name, reference number, and often pulls a photo automatically.
4
Fill in price, purchase date, and condition
These power the Cost-per-Wear metric in Stats. Purchase date is also used to sort your collection.
5
Add straps if the watch has more than one
Expand the Straps section. Add each strap (e.g. "NATO Black", "Oyster Bracelet") and toggle which is currently on the watch — the app will ask which strap you wore each time you log.
Tip: "From Photo" works great for a quick start — snap your watch box and add everything in one go. For the most accurate data, use brand website URLs (rolex.com, omegawatches.com…) with the Fetch button.
Measure Accuracy iOS APP
1
Go to the Measure tab
Select the watch you want to measure and its beat rate (BPH). Leave BPH on Auto if you’re not sure — the app detects it automatically.
2
Place the watch on the microphone
Place the watch touching the iPhone microphone (bottom edge, next to the charging port). The caseback should face the mic. Keep still during measurement.
3
Tap Measure and wait for convergence
Dots appear on the scatter chart as ticks are detected. A preliminary rate shows within seconds, then refines until it converges (usually 30–60 seconds, up to 90). The signal bars in the bottom-left show how strong the signal is.
4
Save or enter manually
Once converged, tap Save to record the reading. You can also enter a rate manually in the Accuracy section of the watch edit form if you measured with an external tool.
5
Trouble getting a reading? Use Advanced Settings
Tap the ⚙ gear (top-right of the Measure screen) to pick an environment preset — Quiet Room, Noisy Environment, or Weak Signal — or adjust Sensitivity and Convergence Speed yourself. Higher Sensitivity helps faint or quiet watches register ticks; these settings can rescue a watch that won’t converge on the defaults.
Tip: Measure in a quiet environment for best results. Watches with display casebacks (transparent backs) produce a stronger signal than solid steel cases.
Logging a Wear
1
Go to the Track tab
The date defaults to today. Tap Yesterday or Pick date to log retroactively. The Today's Pick card suggests a watch based on your rotation — tap Log This Wear to log it directly.
2
Select the watch you wore
Watches are sorted by most recently worn, so the one on your wrist is near the top. Tap to select. If it has multiple straps, a strap picker appears — choose which one was on the watch.
3
Choose a use case and add notes (optional)
Work, Leisure, Dinner, or Travel — use cases power the wear-pattern charts in Stats. Notes are great for occasion details, outfit pairings, or quick impressions.
4
Add a photo and set visibility, then tap "Log This Wear"
Each log can be Public (visible to everyone), Followers (only your followers see it), Close Friends (only your close friends), or Private (only you). The default is set in your Privacy settings.
Logged the wrong watch or use case? Tap the pencil icon on any feed card or in the Wear History table to edit it.
Collection Features
Ranking Game
Tap Ranking Game in the Collection header for head-to-head match-ups. Tap the watch you prefer within 3 seconds. Elo scores accumulate over sessions so your ranking gets more accurate over time.
Tag Filtering
Add tags when editing a watch (Chronograph, Dress Watch, Diver…). Tag chips appear above the grid — tap one to filter, tap again to clear.
Market Prices
Tap Check Value inside any watch to get an AI-powered market estimate, or use the $ button in the collection menu to update all watches at once. You can also enter values manually. Price history is tracked over time.
Per-Watch Privacy
On your profile page, tap any watch in your Collection showcase to cycle its privacy: Public → Followers Only → Close Friends → Private. Private watches are hidden from everyone else.
Post Pics
Toggle Post Pics above the collection grid to swap watch photos for your latest wrist shots. Each card shows the most recent post photo for that watch. Toggle off to go back to the standard watch image.
Wishlist
1
Add watches you want to buy
Paste a URL and Fetch auto-fills the details. Track asking price vs. current market price to spot the right moment to buy.
2
Add from a photo
Tap Add from Photo and snap or pick a picture of a watch you’re after. We’ll identify it and pre-fill the brand, model, and reference — just review and save.
3
Drag to reorder your priority ranking
Grab the drag handle and drag items up or down. The #1 spot is highlighted in gold.
4
Share your wishlist with friends
Go to your profile → Privacy section → set Wishlist to Followers, Close Friends, or Public. Your followers can then see your wishlist on your profile — great for gift inspiration or comparing GAS lists.
Feed & Community
1
Follow or friend other collectors
Tap Find People in the Feed header. Follow anyone — their logs appear in your feed immediately. For Followers Only profiles you need to follow them first to see their collection and wishlist.
2
Post a photo — wear is logged automatically
Tap Post in the Feed header and add a wrist shot. AI identifies the watch from the photo and matches it to your collection. The wear log is added automatically — just tap "Not this watch" if it gets it wrong. Once a watch is tagged, tap Add occasion & strap to record the occasion and which strap you wore. You can also post text-only updates. Edit any post later to change the tagged watch, caption, or photo.
3
Like and comment on posts
Tap the heart to like any post. Tap the comment bubble to read and leave comments. To remove a comment, tap the ⋮ menu on it — you can delete your own comments anywhere, and any comment on your own posts. You'll get a bell notification when someone likes or comments on your posts.
4
Notifications
Tap the bell in the top-right corner to see likes, comments, and follow requests. Tapping a like or comment notification opens the Feed. Tapping a follow request notification lets you accept or decline.
Tip: Pull down on the Feed to refresh. Swipe left or right anywhere to switch between tabs — works across the whole app on mobile.
To unfollow, go to their profile and tap Following → it turns red and asks Unfollow? — tap again to confirm.
Close Friends
1
Send a Close Friend request
On someone's profile, tap the Close Friends button (star icon) to send a request. Both of you must follow each other first.
2
Accept or decline
Close friend requests appear in your notifications bell. Tap Accept to become close friends or Decline to ignore.
3
Close Friends visibility
When logging a wear or posting, you can set visibility to Close Friends. Only people in your close friends circle will see that post.
Close friends is mutual — both people can see each other's close-friends-only content. To remove someone, tap the Close Friends badge on their profile.
Clubs
1
Create or join a club
Go to the Clubs tab and tap Create Club. Give it a name, description, and choose Public or Private. Public clubs allow anyone to join; private clubs require an invite.
2
Invite members
As a club owner, tap Invite Members on the club page to search for users and send invites. You can rescind pending invites at any time.
3
Club posts
When creating a post or logging a wear, select a club to share it with. Club posts appear in the club's feed and are visible to all club members.
4
Manage your club
Tap Manage on your club's page to edit the name, description, photo, and privacy. You can also remove members or delete the club.
@Mentions
—
Mention someone in a comment or post
Type @ followed by a username in any comment or post. A dropdown will appear with matching users — tap one to insert the mention. The mentioned user will receive a notification.
Profile & Privacy
1
Edit your profile
Tap your avatar in the top-right to open your profile, then tap the edit icon to edit your display name, @username, bio, and profile photo.
2
Privacy section — always visible on your profile
Below your edit form you'll find a Privacy card with pill selectors for your privacy settings. Changes save instantly — no Save button needed.
3
Profile visibility
Public — anyone can view your profile and follow you. Followers Only — only people who follow you can see your full profile. Private — hidden from search; no one can view your profile. Changing visibility does not remove existing followers.
4
Collection & Wishlist visibility
Set each independently: Public shows it to anyone who views your profile, Followers shows it only to your followers, Close Friends shows it only to your close friends, Private keeps it hidden from everyone. Wishlist is private by default.
5
Default Post Visibility
Also in the Privacy section — new wear logs and posts default to this visibility (Public, Followers, Close Friends, or Private). You can override it per post when logging.
6
Email Notification Preferences
Expand the Notifications section on your profile to control email alerts. Toggle each category independently: likes & follows, comments, mentions, club activity, and friend requests. Changes save instantly.
7
Recent Posts grid
Below your collection, a 3×3 photo grid shows your latest posts and wears. Photo posts display the photo, wear logs show the watch image, and entries without images show watch initials. Tap any cell to jump to that post in the feed.
Stats
—
Wear frequency & streaks
See how often you wear each watch, your longest streak, and which days of the week you reach for each piece most.
—
Cost per wear
Purchase price divided by total wears — see which watches deliver the most value per outing.
—
Year in Review
A full-year heat-map calendar showing every day you logged a watch. Scroll to the bottom of Stats and select the year.
Streaks
—
Your streak counter
The flame counter in the top bar shows how many days in a row you’ve logged a wear — any log counts. It dims when today isn’t logged yet, so log something to keep it lit.
—
Streak calendar
Tap the streak counter to open a month calendar of every day you logged, with your current and best streak.
—
Streak freezes
Miss a single day and a freeze automatically covers it so your streak survives — frozen days show with an icy tint on the calendar. You start with two and earn one back for every seven days you log. Two missed days in a row still ends the streak.
—
Earn your weekend
Log all five weekdays (Mon–Fri) and you’ve earned the weekend — that Saturday and Sunday won’t break your streak and don’t need logging. They show as a small dot on the calendar, and logging one still counts as a bonus. Miss a weekday that week and the weekend isn’t free.
Achievements
—
Earn badges
Build your collection, log wears, measure accuracy, and keep streaks going to unlock badges. See all of them on your profile under Achievements.
—
Achievements in the feed
When you earn a notable badge it’s shared to your feed — on the post that earned it, or as its own card — so friends can react. Trivial onboarding badges and hidden easter eggs stay private.
—
Control sharing
Don’t want badges in your feed? Turn off “Share achievements to feed” under Profile → Notifications. Badge posts also follow your default post visibility, so a private default never broadcasts.
Safety & Reporting
1
Report a post
Tap the three-dot menu (...) on any post and select Report. Choose a reason (inappropriate, spam, harassment, or other), add optional details, and submit. The content is immediately removed from all feeds while under review.
2
Report a comment
On someone else’s post, tap the three-dot menu and select Report — you’ll see the option to report the post or a specific comment. On your own post, tap the pencil menu and select Report a comment to flag a comment left by another user.
3
Block a user
Tap the three-dot menu on a post and select Block User, or go to their profile and tap Block. Blocked users won’t appear in your feed and cannot interact with your content. You can manage your block list from your profile page.
4
What happens after a report
Reported content is hidden from feeds immediately. An admin reviews every report and either confirms the removal or restores the content. Repeated violations may result in account suspension.
By using WRotate you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy. We have zero tolerance for objectionable content or abusive behaviour.
